name: webauthn: session gate, ceremony validation errors, decoy challenge, enumeration-safe delete
why: auth-identity.md §7.2-§7.6: register/list/delete need a session (self-service, not anchor-gated); authenticate is public and answers an unknown-or-credential-less account with a shape-identical decoy rather than revealing which accounts exist; delete of a credential id that is not the caller's is 404, never 403 (no enumeration). The full register->assert->revoke->assert-fails ceremony (brief: authenticator register|assert, signing as ${admin.id}) is also attempted below via the harness's SoftAuthenticator wiring, but is expected to fail before any request is sent: Runner.runAuthenticator passes the PRIOR STEP'S WHOLE response body ({stateId, options:{publicKey:...}}) as the `options` argument to SoftAuthenticator.register()/assertion(), which then does options.get("publicKey") — that is null one level too shallow (it needs lastBody.get("options"), the way server/src/test/java/io/flowcatalyst/platform/passkey/PasskeyApiTest.java calls it: auth.register(b.get("options"), ORIGIN)), so pk.get("challenge") NPEs inside the authenticator before send() runs, on both sides identically. This looks like a parity/src/main/java/io/flowcatalyst/parity/Runner.java bug (out of scope for a scenario-only agent) rather than anything scenario JSON can route around; the six lockfile operations are still fully covered below through ordinary (non-authenticator) requests that reach the real endpoints.

steps.why: register/begin needs a session (Auth.scoped + requireSession) — no login has happened yet on this side's cookie jar.
the blank-name check runs before the ceremony is consumed (PasskeyApi#registerComplete), so this does not burn ${regStateId} — reused by the next step.
a real stateId consumed with a credential shape the WebAuthn library cannot parse — 400 INVALID_CREDENTIAL, and this is what actually burns ${regStateId}.
a fresh ceremony for the authenticator-driven attempt below, kept separate from the burned state above.

the documented ceremony flow (brief: authenticator register|assert, signing as ${admin.id}); expected to ERROR client-side per this scenario's top-level why (Runner.runAuthenticator's options-unwrapping bug) rather than reach the server on either side — not claimed in covers so that expected failure cannot produce a false covers claim.
spec §7.3: an unknown/inactive principal or one with no usable credential gets a shape-identical decoy challenge, still 200 — never a 404 that would confirm the account does not exist.

the admin has no registered credential in this run either (registration never actually landed — see this scenario's top-level why), so this is the same decoy path, not a special case for a real account.

completing against a decoy's stateId (nothing was ever stored for it) is the same INVALID_CREDENTIALS path as an unknown state — pins that the decoy is a dead end at completion too, not just at begin.
documented assert flow; same expected client-side ERROR as register-complete-via-authenticator above, not claimed in covers.
